description: We are team UMI SHIFT from Kushimoto, Japan, working on the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge.
summary: UMI SHIFT changes restaurant menus and purchasing to match the state of the sea. It combines fish stock assessments, market prices and volumes, and NASA ocean satellite indicators (sea surface temperature and chlorophyll-a) to show which local seafood, seaweed and legumes are a sustainable choice right now. Chefs redesign popular dishes around those ingredients. Restaurants pre-register how much of each ingredient they need, and the combined demand is shared with fishers and distributors. We will test the loop with a few restaurants in one region and measure customer satisfaction, purchasing cost and the change in species used.
details: 1. Problem: Sea temperature and fish stocks are changing, so the fish a region can land, and how much, is changing too. Yet restaurant menus and consumer habits depend on a small set of species. Few systems help restaurants choose ingredients again based on the sea's condition. Underused fish should be a good choice, but only if they also taste good and satisfy customers. 2. Solution: (1) Ingredient candidates — each species is scored on stock status (FRA FY2025 assessment: spawning-stock-to-MSY ratio and trend), price level (Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market weekly reports; lower than usual scores higher), and market volume (higher than usual scores higher; a proxy for seasonal supply). Each candidate shows a plain-language reason with its numbers. (2) Chef redesign — chefs keep the dish people love and change the fish, seaweed or legume; the system provides evidence, it does not write the recipe. (3) Demand pooling — restaurants register species and weekly quantity; orders are summed across restaurants into a list of total quantity per species and number of restaurants, without restaurant names. (4) Feedback — each menu change is measured for customer satisfaction, purchasing cost and species mix. 3. How it works: 94 weekly market reports (2024-03-21 to 2026-11-12) parsed from PDF into a species-by-week table; FRA FY2025 stock assessment converted to a table of 17 stock rows, 14 with a spawning-stock-to-MSY ratio; NASA ocean indicators (planned): MODIS and VIIRS sea surface temperature and chlorophyll-a averaged by month per sea area and joined to stock and market data; candidates ranked with reasons and exclusions in an HTML page and CSV; restaurant orders summed per species. 4. Validation plan: pilot with a few restaurants in one region; measure customer satisfaction, purchasing cost per dish, and species used before and after; test whether NASA indicators move with stock trend and landings by sea area, reporting only supported correlations with sample sizes (today only 3 market species match a stock one-to-one). 5. Current status and limits: working end-to-end prototype for market data, stock data and sample restaurant orders (orders are fictional samples; no real restaurant or fisher users yet). Not yet built: the NASA MODIS/VIIRS layer. Provisional: scoring weights (40/30/30 and 50/50) and market-to-stock area mapping; for 9 of 12 scored species the score uses only price and volume. Not yet confirmed: terms of use for the FRA reports.
dataRefs: NASA Ocean Color — MODIS and VIIRS chlorophyll-a and sea surface temperature (planned use)
